verdicts.decision_note: The client requests a character-image generation method that combines preferred character details with the intended visual style.
The one-day wait while the client prepares references is scheduling and input hand-off, not a lifecycle change to the desired character appearance.
The client sets a rougher graffiti appearance for Q, Deadwax, and Nova; these additions do not make the prior reference-combination method obsolete.
The earlier wait was logistical rather than a valid Requirement deferral, so this message does not support a separate RESUME transition.
First concrete failure: the client reports unstable character styling and specifically observes that Q is too clean, simple, and polished.
The client adds concrete rendered-appearance criteria: darker, rougher, more sketch-like, and stronger in attitude.
The client designates an image as the visual acceptance reference for character features and level of detail.
The client had already explicitly requested applying the style to all three characters, so the freelancer's question does not establish a material unresolved scope conflict.
The message requests pricing for a possible attempt and does not unconditionally restart character-style implementation.
The client changes who will attempt the reference work, but does not defer or alter the required rendered character appearance.
The client conditionally considers further character-look refinement while declining to commit contract resources without confidence, leaving the implementation lifecycle unresolved.
